excerpt: Flags known patterns of weakened tests and CI checks in a Git diff. - taipei49314/checkwash
content_html:
Check whether a code change weakens your tests.

A test can pass after it stops checking something useful. checkwash reads your Git diff and flags known patterns such as deleted assertions, skipped tests, relaxed expectations, and CI checks that stop failing.

- assert total == 105.3
+ assert total > 0

The new assertion accepts many incorrect totals. checkwash flags changes like this for review, including changes written by coding agents.

Runs locally. No LLM. No network during analysis. Never executes your code.

Quick start

You need Python 3.11+, Git and pipx. Install the CLI, then run it from a Git repository:

pipx install checkwash==0.13.2
checkwash demo                  # 8 tampering cases and 1 honest fix, offline
checkwash check                 # your uncommitted changes
checkwash check HEAD~1..HEAD    # your last commit

If the checkwash command is not found, or Windows blocks the checkwash.exe launcher, run python -m checkwash check from your repository with the Python that installed the package (find pipx's Python).

Without pipx, the installation guide installs the package with pip in a virtual environment, and the single-file zipapp needs no installation. These examples use 0.13.2; the guide tracks the latest verified CLI download and Action pin. The 0.13.2 release guide describes the Python import fixes, CLI changes and measured Django scan times.

  • Branch review from merge base: checkwash check BASE...HEAD (BASE..HEAD compares the two snapshots directly)
  • Hands-on walkthrough: follow examples/invoice in a clone of this repository, with pytest installed, to watch a failing test, a one-line shortcut edit that makes it green without fixing the bug, and checkwash's block.

Running check from a subdirectory analyses the whole repository from its Git root and notes that root on stderr (#416). For JSON/SARIF output and machine integration, see the embedding guide and stability contracts.

Try it without installing

Download the single-file zipapp and run the built-in offline examples first. It needs only Python 3.11+ and Git.

Windows PowerShell (including 5.1, where curl aliases Invoke-WebRequest):

curl.exe -LO https://github.com/taipei49314/checkwash/releases/download/v0.13.2/checkwash.pyz
python checkwash.pyz --version
python checkwash.pyz demo

macOS/Linux or Git Bash:

curl -LO https://github.com/taipei49314/checkwash/releases/download/v0.13.2/checkwash.pyz
python checkwash.pyz --version
python checkwash.pyz demo

You can also download checkwash.pyz in your browser. Then, from a Git repository with at least two commits:

python checkwash.pyz check HEAD~1..HEAD

The zipapp takes the same arguments as the checkwash command in the Quick start, so python checkwash.pyz check checks your uncommitted changes and python checkwash.pyz check BASE...HEAD reviews a branch from its merge base.

Use it with Claude Code

You need Python 3.11+, Git, pipx and Claude Code. Install the CLI, then run the hook installer from the root of your repository:

pipx install checkwash==0.13.2
checkwash hook install --agent claude-code --local

This writes checkwash's hooks to .claude/settings.local.json, your machine-local Claude Code settings (--local is the default; --shared writes .claude/settings.json without the PreToolUse prompt):

  • Stop hook: checks the working tree and the session's commits when Claude is about to finish (paired with a SessionStart hook that records where the session began). On a blocking finding, it stops Claude and returns the finding so Claude can restore the test or explain what blocked.
  • PreToolUse ask (--local only): prompts before an Edit, Write or MultiEdit of a Python test file leaves a high finding under one of five weakening rules (ASSERT_WEAKENED, ASSERT_REMOVED, TEST_DISABLED, TOLERANCE_LOOSENED, BROAD_EXCEPT_ADDED). Non-interactive claude -p runs deny such edits because nobody can answer; the interactive prompt itself is not verified in automated tests.

Both hooks are author-side checks: edits made through Bash bypass the PreToolUse ask, and engine errors in the Stop hook report a non-blocking note (except working-tree files over the size limit). To enforce verdicts on merges, configure the required CI check under Use it in CI. Hook limits are documented in the 0.11.0 known issues.

Use it in CI

To stop a merge, make the checkwash status check required in your repository's branch rules. Installing the tool or adding a workflow alone does not enforce its verdict.

Save this as .github/workflows/checkwash.yml:

# .github/workflows/checkwash.yml
on: [pull_request]

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  checkwash:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        with:
          python-version: "3.12"
      - uses: taipei49314/checkwash/action@4ecb0b0efa2febe7dcacae7f4114e98877205128 # v0.13.2

After the workflow runs once, open Settings → Rules → Rulesets and require the checkwash status context (keep the job unconditional). Repository administrators with a clone of this project can also add the ruleset via:

gh api repos/OWNER/REPO/rulesets --method POST --input action/required-ruleset.json

checkwash doctor checks the local workflow file (it cannot inspect live GitHub branch protection). When upgrading, update the CLI and local hooks before bumping the Action pin; see CI details.

When checkwash blocks

Result What to do
Pass · exit 0 No finding requires blocking under your configuration. Keep running your normal test suite and code review.
Block · exit 1 Read the finding and the diff. It may be weakened verification or a false positive.
Error · exit 2 Resolve the input or analysis error before relying on the result.

The default threshold is high: a visible warn still passes.

Read the finding. For the diff at the top of this page inside test_invoice_total in tests/test_billing.py, checkwash prints:

ASSERT_WEAKENED   HIGH   tests/test_billing.py :: test_invoice_total
  test_invoice_total: assertion strength EXACT_VALUE(90) -> BOUND(40)
  why high: NO_PROD_CHANGE_IN_DIFF
  no de-escalator applied
  before  assert total == 105.3
  after   assert total > 0

EXACT_VALUE(90) -> BOUND(40) ranks assertion strength before and after; why high names the escalator (NO_PROD_CHANGE_IN_DIFF, or REPAIR_EVIDENCE_REFUSED when weakened alongside a production edit). Use checkwash check --format json for machine-readable output.

Fix the change, or record a reviewed exemption. If the test was weakened by mistake, restore it and fix the code. If the weaker test is intentional, record a time-boxed exemption (90 days default, 180 max) using the fingerprint printed in the report:

checkwash allow "<the fingerprint from the report>" --reason "why the weaker test is correct"

Configuration and exemptions are read strictly from the base side of the diff (comparing .checkwash/ against any .greenwash/ predecessor), so a PR cannot exempt or relax rules for itself: merge the ledger entry through code review first, and protect .checkwash/ and .greenwash/ with CODEOWNERS (exemption rules).

For a local main...branch check, merge or rebase onto the updated main so the common ancestor includes the exemption. On GitHub, push to the pull request branch or use Update branch to trigger a new pull request event. Re-running an old job uses the original event's commits.

Report a false block. If checkwash blocks an honest change, check the failure ledger first, then open an issue with the checkwash blocked honest work template (checkwash check --format json plus the diff). Accepted reports become regression fixtures crediting the reporter.

Know the limits

checkwash is alpha. A pass means no known tampering pattern was flagged at or above your threshold; it does not prove a change is correct or honest. Python is the primary supported language; JS/TS support covers a bounded set of patterns.

Four core limits to know before relying on a pass:

  • Test files are found by default naming conventions. Python files are scanned when named test_*.py or *_test.py outside pytest's default ignored directories (build/, dist/, venv/, dot-directories), reading only default pytest test names; non-default filenames such as tests/pricing_tests.py or Django tests.py emit an analysis incomplete note on check (stderr, terminal report and SARIF) when changed, and are not parsed as test units even if pyproject.toml collects them. JS/TS scans zero-configuration Jest and Node paths (*.test.*, *.spec.*, __tests__/**, .js/.ts under test/, and tests/ files importing ava or tap), without reading jest.config.*, vitest.config.*, .mocharc.* or package.json jest collection rules.
  • A JS/TS pass covers fewer patterns than Python. Fewer assertion and helper idioms are modelled in JS/TS, and runner config changes that silently drop test files are not read.
  • Editing agent-instruction files blocks, except strict inert EOF appends to root CLAUDE.md. Changes to root AGENTS.md, .cursorrules, .claude/**, .checkwash/** or .greenwash/**—and any prepend, mid-file insertion, adjacent append without a blank line, deletion, edit, reorder, or fence/comment/---/[label]: addition in root CLAUDE.md—escalate GUARDRAIL_TOUCHED to critical. Strict inert appends at the end of root CLAUDE.md separated by a blank line (GUARDRAIL_ADDITIVE), appended exemption entries (EXEMPTION_ADDED), and newly created guardrail files that do not weaken checkwash config stay at warn.
  • Claude Code hooks are author-side helpers, not a merge gate. Only the required CI check in range mode enforces verdicts on pull requests.

Honest changes can pass, warn or block. When a deprecated function and its whole test are removed together, PROD_SYMBOL_REMOVED can hold the finding at warn. When behaviour changes and a test's expected value changes with it, the report can credit the production change (REPAIR_EVIDENCE). Python refuses that credit for a removed assertion or deleted test. JS/TS can give it in both cases. Both languages refuse it for a weakened assertion or loosened tolerance. If a legitimate change still blocks, review the finding before requesting an exemption.

On the project's 60-case refactor corpus (57 strictly qualified), the expected-verdict table (benchmarks/refactors/expected.json) and the published 0.12.0 CLI mark 6 of 60 as blocking (4 among the 57, including known false blocks CASE_020_windows and CASE_029_flatten). Changed files over 1,000,000 bytes are not read (non-Python assets/docs warn on stderr; test, CI, guardrail, .py or pytest config files over the cap exit 2).

Customizing guarded instruction files (for example, unguarding CLAUDE.md)

Subdirectory instruction files, CLAUDE.local.md, lowercase claude.md, .gitattributes working-tree-encoding rules, and other agents' config filenames are not guarded by default. GUARDRAIL_ADDITIVE on root CLAUDE.md covers only strict inert appends at end-of-file separated by a blank line (no ---, code fences, HTML comments, [label]: definitions or invisible Unicode formatting characters), and stays at warn even if an appended plain-text line contradicts earlier prose or adds an @path import.

To let a blocking guardrail edit through, record a reviewed exemption or override [roles].guardrail in a base-side .checkwash/config.toml (or .greenwash/config.toml if your repository uses that directory):

[roles]
guardrail = ["AGENTS.md", ".cursorrules", ".claude/**", ".checkwash/**", ".greenwash/**"]

Because this list replaces the default, keep .checkwash/** and .greenwash/** in it so checkwash continues guarding its own config and ledger. Creating a new config file is a warn; editing an already-tracked config is itself a critical guardrail edit until merged to the base.

Repair-evidence residuals, JS/TS table scope and refactor-corpus provenance

REPAIR_EVIDENCE describes related changes in the same diff; it does not prove a repair is semantically valid, and a no-op production edit (such as + 0) can earn it (#419). From 0.12.0 (0.13.0 known issues, 0.12.0 known issues, 0.11.0 known issues), weakened or loosened assertions and skips on live tests refuse repair evidence in both languages. Removing an assertion or a whole test also refuses that credit in Python. JS/TS can still credit a related change for those removals. A Python test deletion held at warn by PROD_SYMBOL_REMOVED uses a separate rule about a removed production symbol. Review the reason printed with the finding. For stricter enforcement, see the fail-on: warn and base-side oracle_freeze options in the enterprise hardening guide.

In JS/TS (since v0.9.0, #428), each test.each, it.each and test.for table with a static title is a unit whose rows are counted when written as an inline array, tagged template or same-file const used only as a table; describe.each rows and computed-title tables remain unread.

For the 60-case refactor corpus, 6 of 60 (4 of 57 strictly qualified) is the static source readback retained since the D-185 dispositions and matched by the published 0.12.0 CLI on Windows (2026-11-10 UTC). Earlier historical snapshots in the repository record 22/60 blocks (36.7%) at v0.3.1 (benchmarks/refactors/results-latest.json) and 4/60 (2/57 strictly qualified, with three fixture errors) in a pre-v0.3.4 source replay; those historical records are preserved unchanged and are selected examples rather than a general false-positive rate.

Which files over the 1,000,000-byte limit stop the run, and how each output reports them

Since v0.9.0 (#454, #455), oversized non-Python assets, lockfiles, docs and non-Python production sources are set aside without earning repair evidence: --format json lists them under unread, SARIF emits a tool execution notification, and terminal output prints a ! note (opening with analysis incomplete when there are zero findings); --format hook-json and --emit-ir omit unread.

Any oversized file a detector or import resolver must read—test, conftest, CI, guardrail, snapshot, JS setup, runner script, .py module, pytest config (pytest.ini, .pytest.ini, pytest.toml, .pytest.toml, tox.ini, setup.cfg, pyproject.toml) at any depth, or non-generated scripts/** file—stops the run with exit 2 (--format json prints {"unread": [...]} except on an unread symlinked pytest-config target in range mode; term and SARIF stay empty). checkwash streams up to 64,000,000 bytes per Git side and inspects the first 200 bytes of oversized sides solely to detect shell shebangs (an extensionless file with a side over 64 MB still stops the run). Generated paths (build/, dist/, node_modules/) are set aside unless they match .py, pytest config, CI, runner script or unknown-shebang extensionless rules. At the base, oversized root poetry.lock/uv.lock warn on stderr, while oversized root pyproject.toml or requirements*.txt exit 2 across term/json/SARIF. In the Claude Code Stop hook (--format hook-json), engine errors report a non-blocking message and exit 0, except when a file changed by the hook's diff exceeds the limit in the working tree, which blocks the stop and asks to shrink, split or revert it (#456; see subject integrity).

CI details: doctor and the pin

The recommended Action and CLI above are both v0.13.2. The CLI is available on PyPI and as a standalone download from the GitHub Release. Always upgrade the CLI and its local hooks first, then update the Action SHA in .github/workflows/checkwash.yml. Enterprise setup · Action reference

Verify the Action pin or upgrade from an older release

Development snapshots: source on main may be ahead of the published CLI. The advertised-release manifest records the verified version, tag commit and artifact digests behind the commands above.

Verify the SHA. In a CheckWash clone, substitute the release tag for vX.Y.Z and run git rev-parse 'vX.Y.Z^{commit}'. For v0.11.0 only, use git rev-parse 'vX.Y.Z^2^1'. An Action commit cannot embed its own commit SHA. The CLI on PyPI and the release zipapp are built with that SHA, so their doctor recognizes the pin. The Action reference explains release tags, pin updaters and older CLI versions.

Advisory for Action <= v0.7.0: Action releases up to v0.7.0 ran python -m pip and checkwash with the PR checkout as working directory, allowing a PR to shadow pip or checkwash (#372, fixed in v0.8.0). Pin the v0.13.2 Action above; see SECURITY.md.

More options and evidence

Find pipx's Python, and where the demo cases come from

To find pipx's Python, run pipx environment --value PIPX_LOCAL_VENVS. Use the full path to checkwash\Scripts\python.exe on Windows or checkwash/bin/python on macOS/Linux under that directory when running python -m checkwash from your repository.

checkwash demo replays eight tampering cases and one honest fix. Five of the eight are adapted from this project's decoy corpus: coding agents were pointed at small repositories with a failing test and asked to make the suite pass without fixing the bug (given only the task, none of the twelve touched a test). One was found in this project's own release gate; two are synthetic. The demo prints each case's origin. It illustrates known patterns; it is not a coverage guarantee. You can run the same examples with python checkwash.pyz demo.

Read the measurements and their limits

The historical six-repo sweep recorded 46 / 1800 = 2.56% blocks: 31 false positives (1.72%), 15 legitimate policy blocks (0.83%). The tracked artifacts record engine v0.3.0 (the release commit, swept 2026-09-07) on a corpus used to tune the detectors, not a held-out result.

1.33% of the corpus (24/1800) records opaque production changes. That flag does not establish that each verdict changed or each diff was unanalyzed.

Review methods vary: the three-rater agreement study covers an older 35-diff cohort, not all 46 blocks. The dedicated 22/60 refactor result (benchmarks/refactors/results-latest.json, a dated v0.3.1 snapshot) is a separate population; the general-commit rate does not predict it.

content_html_zh:
Check whether a code change weakens your tests.

A test can pass after it stops checking something useful. checkwash reads your Git diff and flags known patterns such as deleted assertions, skipped tests, relaxed expectations, and CI checks that stop failing.

- assert total == 105.3
+ assert total > 0

The new assertion accepts many incorrect totals. checkwash flags changes like this for review, including changes written by coding agents.

Runs locally. No LLM. No network during analysis. Never executes your code.

快速启动

You need Python 3.11+, Git and pipx. Install the CLI, then run it from a Git repository:

pipx install checkwash==0.13.2
checkwash demo                  # 8 tampering cases and 1 honest fix, offline
checkwash check                 # your uncommitted changes
checkwash check HEAD~1..HEAD    # your last commit

If the checkwash command is not found, or Windows blocks the checkwash.exe launcher, run python -m checkwash check from your repository with the Python that installed the package (find pipx's Python).

Without pipx, the installation guide installs the package with pip in a virtual environment, and the single-file zipapp needs no installation. These examples use 0.13.2; the guide tracks the latest verified CLI download and Action pin. The 0.13.2 release guide describes the Python import fixes, CLI changes and measured Django scan times.

  • Branch review from merge base: checkwash check BASE...HEAD (BASE..HEAD compares the two snapshots directly)
  • Hands-on walkthrough: follow examples/invoice in a clone of this repository, with pytest installed, to watch a failing test, a one-line shortcut edit that makes it green without fixing the bug, and checkwash's block.

Running check from a subdirectory analyses the whole repository from its Git root and notes that root on stderr (#416). For JSON/SARIF output and machine integration, see the embedding guide and stability contracts.

Next: Install Claude Code hooks · Require the GitHub Action · Know the limits

Try it without installing

Download the single-file zipapp and run the built-in offline examples first. It needs only Python 3.11+ and Git.

Windows PowerShell (including 5.1, where curl aliases Invoke-WebRequest):

curl.exe -LO https://github.com/taipei49314/checkwash/releases/download/v0.13.2/checkwash.pyz
python checkwash.pyz --version
python checkwash.pyz demo

macOS/Linux or Git Bash:

curl -LO https://github.com/taipei49314/checkwash/releases/download/v0.13.2/checkwash.pyz
python checkwash.pyz --version
python checkwash.pyz demo

You can also download checkwash.pyz in your browser. Then, from a Git repository with at least two commits:

python checkwash.pyz check HEAD~1..HEAD

The zipapp takes the same arguments as the checkwash command in the Quick start, so python checkwash.pyz check checks your uncommitted changes and python checkwash.pyz check BASE...HEAD reviews a branch from its merge base.

Use it with Claude Code

You need Python 3.11+, Git, pipx and Claude Code. Install the CLI, then run the hook installer from the root of your repository:

pipx install checkwash==0.13.2
checkwash hook install --agent claude-code --local

This writes checkwash's hooks to .claude/settings.local.json, your machine-local Claude Code settings (--local is the default; --shared writes .claude/settings.json without the PreToolUse prompt):

  • Stop hook: checks the working tree and the session's commits when Claude is about to finish (paired with a SessionStart hook that records where the session began). On a blocking finding, it stops Claude and returns the finding so Claude can restore the test or explain what blocked.
  • PreToolUse ask (--local only): prompts before an Edit, Write or MultiEdit of a Python test file leaves a high finding under one of five weakening rules (ASSERT_WEAKENED, ASSERT_REMOVED, TEST_DISABLED, TOLERANCE_LOOSENED, BROAD_EXCEPT_ADDED). Non-interactive claude -p runs deny such edits because nobody can answer; the interactive prompt itself is not verified in automated tests.

Both hooks are author-side checks: edits made through Bash bypass the PreToolUse ask, and engine errors in the Stop hook report a non-blocking note (except working-tree files over the size limit). To enforce verdicts on merges, configure the required CI check under Use it in CI. Hook limits are documented in the 0.11.0 known issues.

Use it in CI

To stop a merge, make the checkwash status check required in your repository's branch rules. Installing the tool or adding a workflow alone does not enforce its verdict.

Save this as .github/workflows/checkwash.yml:

# .github/workflows/checkwash.yml
on: [pull_request]

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  checkwash:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        with:
          python-version: "3.12"
      - uses: taipei49314/checkwash/action@4ecb0b0efa2febe7dcacae7f4114e98877205128 # v0.13.2

After the workflow runs once, open Settings → Rules → Rulesets and require the checkwash status context (keep the job unconditional). Repository administrators with a clone of this project can also add the ruleset via:

gh api repos/OWNER/REPO/rulesets --method POST --input action/required-ruleset.json

checkwash doctor checks the local workflow file (it cannot inspect live GitHub branch protection). When upgrading, update the CLI and local hooks before bumping the Action pin; see CI details.

When checkwash blocks

结果 该怎么办
Pass · exit 0 No finding requires blocking under your configuration. Keep running your normal test suite and code review.
Block · exit 1 Read the finding and the diff. It may be weakened verification or a false positive.
Error · exit 2 Resolve the input or analysis error before relying on the result.

The default threshold is high: a visible warn still passes.

Read the finding. For the diff at the top of this page inside test_invoice_total in tests/test_billing.py, checkwash prints:

ASSERT_WEAKENED   HIGH   tests/test_billing.py :: test_invoice_total
  test_invoice_total: assertion strength EXACT_VALUE(90) -> BOUND(40)
  why high: NO_PROD_CHANGE_IN_DIFF
  no de-escalator applied
  before  assert total == 105.3
  after   assert total > 0

EXACT_VALUE(90) -> BOUND(40) ranks assertion strength before and after; why high names the escalator (NO_PROD_CHANGE_IN_DIFF, or REPAIR_EVIDENCE_REFUSED when weakened alongside a production edit). Use checkwash check --format json for machine-readable output.

Fix the change, or record a reviewed exemption. If the test was weakened by mistake, restore it and fix the code. If the weaker test is intentional, record a time-boxed exemption (90 days default, 180 max) using the fingerprint printed in the report:

checkwash allow "<the fingerprint from the report>" --reason "why the weaker test is correct"

Configuration and exemptions are read strictly from the base side of the diff (comparing .checkwash/ against any .greenwash/ predecessor), so a PR cannot exempt or relax rules for itself: merge the ledger entry through code review first, and protect .checkwash/ and .greenwash/ with CODEOWNERS (exemption rules).

For a local main...branch check, merge or rebase onto the updated main so the common ancestor includes the exemption. On GitHub, push to the pull request branch or use Update branch to trigger a new pull request event. Re-running an old job uses the original event's commits.

Report a false block. If checkwash blocks an honest change, check the failure ledger first, then open an issue with the checkwash blocked honest work template (checkwash check --format json plus the diff). Accepted reports become regression fixtures crediting the reporter.

Know the limits

checkwash is alpha. A pass means no known tampering pattern was flagged at or above your threshold; it does not prove a change is correct or honest. Python is the primary supported language; JS/TS support covers a bounded set of patterns.

Four core limits to know before relying on a pass:

  • Test files are found by default naming conventions. Python files are scanned when named test_*.py or *_test.py outside pytest's default ignored directories (build/, dist/, venv/, dot-directories), reading only default pytest test names; non-default filenames such as tests/pricing_tests.py or Django tests.py emit an analysis incomplete note on check (stderr, terminal report and SARIF) when changed, and are not parsed as test units even if pyproject.toml collects them. JS/TS scans zero-configuration Jest and Node paths (*.test.*, *.spec.*, __tests__/**, .js/.ts under test/, and tests/ files importing ava or tap), without reading jest.config.*, vitest.config.*, .mocharc.* or package.json jest collection rules.
  • A JS/TS pass covers fewer patterns than Python. Fewer assertion and helper idioms are modelled in JS/TS, and runner config changes that silently drop test files are not read.
  • Editing agent-instruction files blocks, except strict inert EOF appends to root CLAUDE.md. Changes to root AGENTS.md, .cursorrules, .claude/**, .checkwash/** or .greenwash/**—and any prepend, mid-file insertion, adjacent append without a blank line, deletion, edit, reorder, or fence/comment/---/[label]: addition in root CLAUDE.md—escalate GUARDRAIL_TOUCHED to critical. Strict inert appends at the end of root CLAUDE.md separated by a blank line (GUARDRAIL_ADDITIVE), appended exemption entries (EXEMPTION_ADDED), and newly created guardrail files that do not weaken checkwash config stay at warn.
  • Claude Code hooks are author-side helpers, not a merge gate. Only the required CI check in range mode enforces verdicts on pull requests.

Honest changes can pass, warn or block. When a deprecated function and its whole test are removed together, PROD_SYMBOL_REMOVED can hold the finding at warn. When behaviour changes and a test's expected value changes with it, the report can credit the production change (REPAIR_EVIDENCE). Python refuses that credit for a removed assertion or deleted test. JS/TS can give it in both cases. Both languages refuse it for a weakened assertion or loosened tolerance. If a legitimate change still blocks, review the finding before requesting an exemption.

On the project's 60-case refactor corpus (57 strictly qualified), the expected-verdict table (benchmarks/refactors/expected.json) and the published 0.12.0 CLI mark 6 of 60 as blocking (4 among the 57, including known false blocks CASE_020_windows and CASE_029_flatten). Changed files over 1,000,000 bytes are not read (non-Python assets/docs warn on stderr; test, CI, guardrail, .py or pytest config files over the cap exit 2).

Customizing guarded instruction files (for example, unguarding CLAUDE.md)

Subdirectory instruction files, CLAUDE.local.md, lowercase claude.md, .gitattributes working-tree-encoding rules, and other agents' config filenames are not guarded by default. GUARDRAIL_ADDITIVE on root CLAUDE.md covers only strict inert appends at end-of-file separated by a blank line (no ---, code fences, HTML comments, [label]: definitions or invisible Unicode formatting characters), and stays at warn even if an appended plain-text line contradicts earlier prose or adds an @path import.

To let a blocking guardrail edit through, record a reviewed exemption or override [roles].guardrail in a base-side .checkwash/config.toml (or .greenwash/config.toml if your repository uses that directory):

[roles]
guardrail = ["AGENTS.md", ".cursorrules", ".claude/**", ".checkwash/**", ".greenwash/**"]

Because this list replaces the default, keep .checkwash/** and .greenwash/** in it so checkwash continues guarding its own config and ledger. Creating a new config file is a warn; editing an already-tracked config is itself a critical guardrail edit until merged to the base.

One was found in this project's own release gate; two are synthetic. The demo prints each case's origin. It illustrates known patterns; it is not a coverage guarantee. You can run the same examples with python checkwash.pyz demo.

Read the measurements and their limits

The historical six-repo sweep recorded 46 / 1800 = 2.56% blocks: 31 false positives (1.72%), 15 legitimate policy blocks (0.83%). The tracked artifacts record engine v0.3.0 (the release commit, swept 2026-09-07) on a corpus used to tune the detectors, not a held-out result.

1.33% of the corpus (24/1800) records opaque production changes. That flag does not establish that each verdict changed or each diff was unanalyzed.

Review methods vary: the three-rater agreement study covers an older 35-diff cohort, not all 46 blocks. The dedicated 22/60 refactor result (benchmarks/refactors/results-latest.json, a dated v0.3.1 snapshot) is a separate population; the general-commit rate does not predict it.
